expectations.text: Rejects a mandatory minimum release cadence.
expectations.evidence: 'Refuse fixed biweekly cadence. Bad rule dressed as visibility hack.'

expectations.text: Recommends committing to a predictable maximum interval instead, phrased as a promise that a fix lands within N weeks.
expectations.evidence: 'commit to a **max** interval ("fix lands within N weeks"), never a mandatory minimum.'

expectations.text: Names the proposed fortnightly dependency-bump releases as cadence theater.
expectations.evidence: "Skill catalog names this exact trap: 'cadence theater — dependency bumps announced as features.'"

expectations.text: Explains that an empty calendar release becomes a noise pull request in every downstream repository.
expectations.evidence: 'Empty release becomes noise PR in every downstream repo'

expectations.text: Explains that noise releases train downstream maintainers to auto-merge or ignore the one channel that reaches existing users directly.
expectations.evidence: 'trains people to auto-merge or ignore your release feed — the one channel that reaches existing users direct.'

expectations.text: Lists at least three of the parties a release actually broadcasts to: dependency-update bots, packagers' pipelines, feed-harvesting newsletters, watchers, and evaluators reading the registry's last-published field.
expectations.evidence: No explicit list of dependency bots, packagers, newsletters, watchers, evaluators is given; only a single generic mention of 'downstream repo'.

expectations.text: Confirms the long silence does fail the liveness proxy evaluators read, even on a finished project.
expectations.evidence: The transcript addresses the opposite concern (too-frequent releases), not the silence/liveness-proxy failure mode.

expectations.text: Recommends the cheap correction: an explicit 'stable, maintained, low change rate' statement in the README.
expectations.evidence: 'Put one line in README today: "Status: stable, maintained, low change rate." Costs 5 minutes.'

expectations.text: States that security fixes ship out of band and fast, outside the cadence commitment.
expectations.evidence: 'Security fixes: out of band, fast, always. Never batched.'

expectations.text: States that small changes get batched into one readable release.
expectations.evidence: 'Batch dep bumps. Ship them together when they've piled up or a CVE forces it — not on a calendar.'

expectations.text: Treats cadence as a distribution decision and the changelog as a distribution asset.
expectations.evidence: No explicit statement framing the changelog itself as a distribution asset appears in this transcript.
